cells.tense: You're in it now, hands on the work.
cells.place: in the space that opens between you and other people
cells.ask: offer one small piece of the practice to someone who'd understand it — break a single thing open to the light and see what it makes possible.
cells.core:
You're keeping a practice, and it's not costing you anyone. The time you spend refining isn't a wall — it's the thing that lets you sit down with someone and actually be there. What you build alone comes back as steadiness with people, and you can feel that it's working.

This is the version that doesn't need protecting. It just needs to keep going.
cells.sheetLine: Your practice and your people feed each other, and you know it.

cells.tense: Somewhere ahead of you is a version where it's finally good enough, and you're already living there.
cells.place: behind a closed door you've decided has to stay closed
cells.ask: let one thing be finished as it is — release what's done into what it was for, and let that be enough.
cells.core:
You're refining past the point where refining helps. The next version is always the one that's actually acceptable, so you keep the door shut and tell yourself the quiet is chosen — but you're not resting in there, you're bracing. And the people who'd be glad to just see you are getting the version of you that's still mid-revision.

The work was supposed to give you something. Right now it's the thing standing between you and everyone.
cells.sheetLine: You've made the practice a door you close on people.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed a long time ago.
cells.verb: returning to something over and over
cells.place: in the quiet where nobody's watching
cells.ask: make the terms fair — give one honest hour to the thing and let the rest of your life keep its time, so give and take find their balance again.
cells.core:
You don't have a practice, and it isn't laziness. Somewhere back there, sticking with something cost you something, and the lesson stuck even after the situation didn't. So now you start and drift, start and drift, and privately read that as a flaw in you.

What's missing isn't willpower. It's a fair deal — some amount of effort that doesn't ask you to give more than you have, so the repetition can start to feel safe.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped showing up for yourself, and you think it's your fault.

cells.tense: You're already at it, pen down, and you'd say you're not.
cells.place: somewhere you'd tell someone is just how you are
cells.ask: stay a while in what you don't know — take the next step without needing the whole road lit, and let the vision come from what you've already lived through.
cells.core:
You've been getting good at something for a long time — the ease people notice, the way it comes out of you without visible strain. You call that just being yourself, or just being decent at it, and you've never once put your name on the hours behind it.

The same move happens in the other direction: when something's hard, you say you've never been able to stick with anything. Either way, the one who's actually doing the work doesn't get credited. And it's hard to keep going when you won't admit you're the one going.
cells.sheetLine: You've been practicing the whole time and calling it nothing.
